title: Strictness of the polynomial hierarchy
formal: For every integer \(k\ge0\), is \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\subsetneq\Sigma_{k+1}^{\mathrm P}\)? In other words, must each additional fixed block of polynomially bounded alternating Boolean quantifiers enable a decision language that cannot be expressed with k blocks? The classes are the uniform, unrelativized classes defined below.
definitions: All languages are subsets of \(\{0,1\}^*\); membership is a total yes/no decision on every finite binary string. Let \(\Sigma_0^{\mathrm P}=\Pi_0^{\mathrm P}=\mathrm P\), where P consists of languages decided by a single deterministic multitape Turing machine within \(C(n+1)^d\) transitions on every length-n string, for fixed integers \(C\ge1,d\ge0\). Machines have a finite program, fixed finite alphabets, a read-only input and initially blank work tapes; each transition reads or writes at the heads and moves each head by at most one cell. For fixed \(k\ge1\), a language L belongs to \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\) if there exist integers \(a\ge1,b\ge0\) and one deterministic polynomial-time Boolean predicate R such that for every x, with \(n=|x|\) and \(p(n)=a(n+1)^b\), \(x\in L\iff\exists y_1\in\{0,1\}^{p(n)}\ \forall y_2\in\{0,1\}^{p(n)}\cdots Q_k y_k\in\{0,1\}^{p(n)}\ R(x,y_1,\ldots,y_k)=1\). Here \(Q_i\) is existential for odd i and universal for even i. An entire string is chosen in each block; k does not count individual quantified bits. To fix the predicate input, encode a tuple by concatenating \(1^{|s|}0s\) for each of its k+1 components in order. R is computed by one machine in the model above, halting within \(C(M+1)^d\) on all length-M strings for fixed C,d and rejecting malformed tuple encodings. Runtime counts all transitions and all input bits. Restricting the common witness bound to this form of p loses no languages, because a larger polynomial bound can pad each witness and ignore unused bits. The integers, machines and time bounds may depend on L and on the fixed k, but not on x or the quantified strings. Define \(\Pi_k^{\mathrm P}=\{\{0,1\}^*\setminus L:L\in\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\}\) and \(\mathrm{PH}=\bigcup_{k\ge0}\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\). Thus \(\Sigma_1^{\mathrm P}=\mathrm{NP}\) and \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm P}=\mathrm{coNP}\). No advice, random bits, quantum operations, external oracle or promise inputs are present. The inclusion between consecutive existential levels always holds; strictness means that there exists a language \(L_k\in\Sigma_{k+1}^{\mathrm P}\setminus\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}\). This language may depend on k; there is no added requirement of an effective generator for all separating languages.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of strict containment for every nonnegative integer k, or prove that \(\Sigma_k^{\mathrm P}=\Sigma_{k+1}^{\mathrm P}\) for some fixed nonnegative integer k. The negative answer is exactly the logical negation, since the inclusions are unconditional. Equality at one adjacent pair collapses all higher finite levels. A separation of finitely many initial levels, an oracle separation, or a collapse conditional on an unproved hypothesis is insufficient to settle the displayed all-level assertion. No concrete finite input is required as a witness to a class equality or separation.
why: This is the organizing conjecture behind the computational cost of alternating existential and universal reasoning. It strengthens the basic P-versus-NP distinction across all fixed quantifier depths and underlies many conditional lower bounds in complexity, verification, and graph problems with nested solution requirements.

importance.reason: A foundational conjecture asserting that every further alternation increases computational power. It governs a large family of complexity classifications and has major circuit-lower-bound consequences.

progress.text: Meyer and Stockmeyer introduce the hierarchy, and Stockmeyer develops its structure and complete problems. The source survey traces this history and gives the quantified-predicate definition used here.

Karp–Lipton relates polynomial-size circuits for NP to a collapse of PH; Yao and Håstad establish infinitude in a suitably chosen oracle world. These concern a conditional implication and a relativized separation, respectively.
Rossman, Servedio and Tan prove that a random oracle gives an infinite polynomial hierarchy with probability one. Each binary string independently belongs to that oracle with probability one half.
Wigderson’s book still states strictness of successive unrelativized levels as a conjecture and distinguishes fixed-depth quantification from unrestricted polynomial-space reasoning.

Hirsch and Volkovich’s revised paper compares classes associated with the Linear Ordering Principle and strengthens Karp–Lipton-style conditional conclusions. Its assumptions do not establish an unconditional collapse of PH.

status_note: The strictness conjecture is explicit in the checked 2015 survey and 2019 book. The checked 2026 revision supplies conditional collapses and related containments, while the 2015 theorem is relativized. A bounded primary-source search on 14 September 2026 found no verified unconditional resolution; this review checks statement scope rather than independently certifying every proof.

context_blocks.text: NP captures a single existential choice of a certificate. A second block permits a statement of the form “there is a candidate that survives every challenge”; a third permits a response to every challenge. Polynomially many bits may be chosen at each stage. The question is whether every additional fixed stage enables some decision problem that cannot be expressed with fewer stages and a polynomial-time final check.

The hierarchy is monotone because an additional unused block is harmless. Equality of neighboring levels would make all subsequent levels equal as well, a standard collapse property of bounded alternation. Thus the negative answer asserts a finite level at which the hierarchy stabilizes; it does not require separating or collapsing every level independently.

Strictness includes \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{NP}\) at its first step, but \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{NP}\) alone would leave the possibility of a later collapse. The conjecture also implies that PH is a proper subclass of PSPACE: if TQBF belonged to PH, it would belong to one fixed level, and PSPACE-completeness would force the whole hierarchy into that level. Allowing arbitrarily many quantifier alternations in the input is therefore a separate issue from allowing any fixed number.

The Karp–Lipton implication connects this conjecture to circuit complexity. Polynomial-size circuits for NP would collapse PH, so an infinite hierarchy would imply an NP language without polynomial-size circuits. Conditional collapse arguments are useful precisely because they can turn an assumption about nonuniform circuits into a conclusion about uniform classes; the conditional conclusion is not an established collapse.

Rossman, Servedio, and Tan prove that PH is infinite relative to a random oracle with probability one, through an average-case circuit-depth hierarchy theorem. Random membership bits supplied by an oracle are an extra computational resource. The result shows that strictness is compatible with, and typical in, that oracle model; it leaves the unrelativized hierarchy open.

The quantifier count is fixed separately for each class. It does not describe an algorithm that receives an arbitrary level number and solves all those levels with one common polynomial bound. Similarly, strictness may use a different separating language at every level, and the statement does not impose a uniform procedure generating all such languages.

sentences: The polynomial hierarchy classifies decision languages by a fixed number of alternating existential and universal blocks.
Each block chooses polynomially many bits, followed by a uniform polynomial-time check.
The question asks whether every added block strictly increases the class of expressible languages.
Equality of any neighboring levels would make the entire hierarchy stabilize at a finite level.
Known oracle separations and conditional collapses reveal consequences and barriers while leaving this unrelativized conjecture unresolved.
